correctness.notes: oracle passed on every measured cell | phase 3 final evaluation, harness 0.10, nodes gb200-nvl4-ts2-99

low_level: Registers 62 to 255 over the 177 distinct kernels behind the card's cells (41 with register spills, a kernel measured in more than one batch counts once), shared memory 8560 to 168400 bytes, harness 0.10 on gb200-nvl4-ts2-99.
Adapter statics: input arrangement striped, output indices, temp storage 8528 to 135632 bytes.
Oracle battery (23 cases per cell plus the measurement seeds) passed on every cell that has a number, no cell unsupported, no cell failed the oracle.
algorithmic: Random input (the one-node matrix on gb200-nvl4-ts2-99): latency not_guaranteed wins 4 of 45 cells (runner-up in 2), latency prefer_smaller_index wins 3 of 43 cells (runner-up in 2), throughput not_guaranteed wins 5 of 52 cells (runner-up in 1), throughput prefer_smaller_index wins 2 of 42 cells (runner-up in 1).
Where it wins on random input (fp32 N 8192, fp32 N 32768), the median margin over the runner-up is +105 percent and over the scope's reference control +237 percent.

Largest random-input deficits (distinct cells, worst regime): bf16 N 1024 k 4 +692 percent behind B2_packed@T128 in throughput prefer_smaller_index, bf16 N 4096 k 4 +512 percent behind B2_twolevel in latency prefer_smaller_index, bf16 N 1024 k 8 +452 percent behind B2_packed@T128 in throughput prefer_smaller_index, fp32 N 1024 k 4 +370 percent behind B2_packed@T128 in throughput prefer_smaller_index.

Named workloads won on random input: beam_search_chunk, dsa_v4_flash_chunk_32k_k512, dsa_v4_pro_chunk_32k_k1024, eagle_vocab_topk_sglang, quest_pages_128k_budget4096, sampling_chunk_32k_k64, snapkv_32k_budget1024.
negative: The GB200 pass measured random input only on one host (gb200-nvl4-ts2-99): the tie_heavy, shuffled-tie and phase 3b order-check findings for this adapter are on its B200 card. On B200 the aligned tie_heavy pattern sends B4_v4 to its tile fallback, a code property that holds on this host too.
surprises: None beyond what the tables show.
open_questions: A cheaper fallback detection for tie floods (count the bound's ties before running the full tile path) and whether k = N/4 can be rescued by a second bound.

B200 pass (WINNERS_b200.md, random input on umbriel-b200-047, tie_heavy on 068, shuffled ties on 094, phase 3b on 047): the warp and sub-warp winners agree with GB200 on 359 of 376 common cells (365 of 376 when each cell is compared through the adapters both passes measured, as section 16 of the knowledge base does), the differences are named sub-warp lane-count cells, N 128 sub-warp throughput cells and warp ties within 5 percent, and in the block matrices the B1_idx against B1_det2 throughput ties fall either way. On GB200 the k 64 cells at 128 threads run 3 to 15 percent slower than on B200 (hw-researcher, a generation property) and the aarch64 cicc emits branches for the conditional swaps (T20, 3 to 4 percent).
